record.original_question: Does there exist a root-finding method, for instance among generalizations of Newton, Konig, or Chebyshev type methods, whose Fatou set contains a Herman ring?

evidence.quote: To our knowledge, no root-finding method is known to possess a Herman ring in the Fatou set. The same is also true whenever f is an entire function.
Certain root-finding techniques are known to have disconnected Julia sets. This raises the question of whether there is a root-finding method whose Fatou set contains a Herman ring.

artifact.status_search_result: No root-finding method (Newton, König, Chebyshev or known generalizations) is currently known to admit a Herman ring in its Fatou set; for Newton's method applied to polynomials the Julia set is connected, ruling out Herman rings, while for König's and Chebyshev's methods the existence of Herman rings is neither proved nor ruled out. The question is reported as open in recent surveys on Herman rings.

status_evidence.title: Herman Rings: Structure, Dynamics, and Open Problems
status_evidence.snippet: To our knowledge, no root-finding method is known to possess a Herman ring in the Fatou set.
status_evidence.claim: The existence of a root-finding method whose Fatou set contains a Herman ring is stated as an open question.

status_evidence.title: On König's root-finding algorithms (Buff–Henriksen)
status_evidence.snippet: Study of dynamics of König's methods as generalizations of Newton's method.
status_evidence.claim: König's methods are studied dynamically but no Herman ring example is exhibited.
